task.name: Routing selects models without checking whether the active account can call them
task.story_text:
## Why

Routing picks a model from the configured pool on price, tier and capability. It
does not ask whether the account the run will dispatch with is permitted to call
that model, so a model the provider has withdrawn stays selectable until a story
dispatches to it and is refused.

That happened on 2026-09-04. OpenAI withdrew `gpt-5.4` from Codex under
ChatGPT-account authentication on 2026-08-31. Routing selected it for dev in two
repositories eight minutes apart; both were refused in five seconds with
`HTTP 400 — The 'gpt-5.4' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT
account`, after WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan had already run and been
paid for. Four stories produced nothing.

Forge already declines to route a model recorded as withdrawn: a `status:
retired` catalog entry carries `dev_capable=False` and empty
`phase_eligibility`, and naming it in `forge.yaml` fails at load with the reason.
Two DeepSeek entries work exactly that way today. The record driving it is
hand-maintained, so the guard fires only for withdrawals a human already found.

A static record is also not sufficient here, and this is what distinguishes this
issue from marking one more entry retired. Availability is a property of the
model *and the credentials in use*: `gpt-5.4` remains callable through Codex
under API-key authentication and is refused only under ChatGPT-account
authentication. No fixed per-identifier status can express that, because the
answer differs by how the run authenticates.

The information needed is already available locally and free. The Codex package
forge pins answers `debug models` from the signed-in account's own catalog with
no generative call, and that catalog does not list `gpt-5.4`. Forge also already
knows it does not know: `check-config` reports `never checked against the
provider's published model list` for every OpenAI profile configured on the
machine, including the ones dev now routes to.

Scope note: this issue is the routing behavior only — which models are eligible,
and withholding one the provider has refused. The readiness *report* that calls
launcher presence "ready" is fuzzypete/theforge#2909. Classifying a refused call's cost as zero
rather than unknown is fuzzypete/theforge#2913.

## Acceptance criteria

Every configured model resolves to exactly one of three states, and the states
are not interchangeable:

- **available** — the account's own list of invocable models includes it. It
  routes normally.
- **unavailable** — that list exists and does not include it. It is logged and
  excluded from selection; routing proceeds with the remaining models.
- **unverified** — no list could be obtained for that provider, or the attempt
  to obtain one failed. **It remains fully eligible for routing**, and the run
  warns once that its availability is unconfirmed. Unverified is never treated
  as unavailable: a provider that publishes no catalog must keep working exactly
  as it does today, and a network failure or an expired login must never disable
  a provider that was serving traffic a minute earlier.

Beyond the three states:

- Availability is resolved for the account and authentication mode the run will
  dispatch with. The same identifier may be available under one auth mode and
  unavailable under another, so nothing records availability as a fixed property
  of the identifier.
- A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any
  spend, naming which models were excluded and why.
- Resolution completes without dispatching a generative request and without the
  operator running anything.
- When a dispatch is nonetheless refused for a reason that is a property of the
  configuration rather than the request — the account may not call this model —
  that model is quarantined for the remainder of the run. No later story, phase
  or role routes to it, and the run continues on the remaining models rather than
  meeting the identical refusal once per story. This applies to an unverified
  model as much as to one the list claimed was available: an explicit refusal is
  stronger evidence than any prior state, and it is what converts unverified into
  unavailable for the rest of that run.
- Entries already marked withdrawn by hand in the packaged catalog remain
  non-routable. Both sources converge on the same outcome; neither overrides the
  other toward availability.
- An availability answer carries the time it was obtained, and one older than the
  existing identity-verification window is refreshed or reported as stale rather
  than reused as current.

## Example

Today, `gpt-5.4` withdrawn upstream and still in the pool:

```
$ forge check-config
    openai/gpt-5.4/cli              never checked against the provider's published model list
  openai-gpt-5.4-cli    openai    cli:codex gpt-5.4     budget=$2.00  ✓ ready

$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  [DEV] FAIL | exit=1 | cost=unknown
  error output: {"status":400,"error":{"message":"The 'gpt-5.4' model is not
  supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
  ✗ ESCALATE   Dev agent failed and produced no commits ahead of base
```

Wanted:

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded — not available to this account under
             codex ChatGPT-account auth (account catalog, checked 2026-09-05)
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4-mini  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.42  4m 11s
```

And where nothing remains:

```
$ forge sprint --issues 2775 ...
  ✗ ROUTING  no model available for phase dev: openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded
             (not available to this account), openai/gpt-5.5/cli excluded
             (not available to this account). Nothing dispatched, $0.00 spent.
```

- [P1] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 still runs rerouting only before a future dispatch. After an unsuccessful entitlement refusal, dev_phase.py::_run_dev_phase enters its ordinary failed-result handling and engine.py's DEV startup/failure guards terminate the story; plan_flow.py likewise returns an escalation immediately when PLAN fails. No step intercepts MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE after the result and loops the same phase, so no next dispatch exists on which reroute_for_quarantine can act.
  Suggestion: In each phase owner, intercept MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE immediately after the result, reroute, and redispatch the same phase without consuming a normal model/review retry or recording model judgment. Convert to a routing stop only when reselection proves the phase empty.
- [P1] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 names preflight._escalate_dev_model as the reseating mechanism. That function selects only a dev-capable model with strictly greater capability than the incumbent, so it cannot choose a surviving lower-ranked model such as the specification's gpt-5.4-mini example. It also cannot select replacements for PLAN or reviewer roles.
  Suggestion: Re-run the authoritative assignment machinery against the quarantine-filtered candidates, or introduce a phase-generic selector that preserves pins and pool ordering while allowing any normally eligible surviving candidate.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 assumes NoAvailableModelError raised before DEV or REVIEW dispatch automatically becomes the existing SKIPPED routing outcome. In engine.py, the _coordinator_loop calls are generally guarded only for StoryCancelled; existing NoAvailableModelError catches surround preflight, plan, checkpoint, and restore boundaries. A later DEV/reviewer reroute exception therefore escapes to sprint worker failure handling instead of producing ROUTING_STOPPED_ERROR_TYPE.
  Suggestion: Add a shared engine-level conversion around every _coordinator_loop entry, or return an explicit routing-stop result from the phase owners, preserving the named exclusions and preventing capability or assignment-history writes.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan explicitly carries the risk that only runner_codex.py emits MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE. Equivalent account/model entitlement refusals from API, Claude, Gemini, or gh-aw remain ordinary failures and never enter quarantine, despite the acceptance criterion being transport-neutral. Step 3's observer tests can only observe a code supplied by a fake; they do not add real classifiers for those transports.
  Suggestion: Add narrow classifiers for supported transports' stable entitlement-refusal responses, or formally narrow the acceptance criterion before implementation.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 still describes constructing the all-quarantined synthetic result through the existing _capability_refusal_result pattern. That function hard-codes SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED, which mislabels account entitlement as a capability gap even if failure_code is replaced.
  Suggestion: Create a dedicated account-unavailability result constructor with its own marker, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE, startup_failure=True, and cost_usd=None; test that it produces a routing skip and no capability evidence.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 checks runtime_dispatch_key parity only after transport fallback has already been applied. profile_dispatch_key applies config.transport_fallbacks itself, so an as-received pre-fallback profile can be quarantined under a key the catalog overlay does not use.
  Suggestion: Normalize before deriving the runtime key, or prove every run_agent caller supplies a normalized profile and add a parity test using a profile whose configured transport fallback has not yet been applied.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 states that a NoAvailableModelError raised from a phase owner 'is the routing stop the criterion asks for' via existing behaviour. It is not, at the new call sites: engine.py catches that exception only at the cached-preflight application (engine.py:1473, 1944), the post-plan checkpoint (1604) and the resume re-derivation (2044), plus preflight_flow.py:475/1225. A raise from reroute_for_quarantine before a second DEV iteration or a review-pool retry travels out through _coordinator_loop (which catches only StoryCancelled) and is recorded FAILED by the sprint worker's generic handler.
  Suggestion: Wrap the new mid-story call sites with the same conversion the existing boundaries use — routing_stop_message(exc, state.total_cost_measured) into a CoordinatorResult with the routing-stop error type and no capability/assignment history — or add one conversion around every _coordinator_loop entry. Step 6's nothing-left test should raise from a later-phase pass, not from initial routing, so it actually exercises this.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 names _escalate_dev_model for reselecting a quarantined phase profile. That helper (preflight.py:907) returns 'the lowest-capability model that is still higher than current' and filters on dev_capable — it cannot express the story's own gpt-5.4 → gpt-5.4-mini reseat (the survivor is lower-capability), and it has no equivalent for plan, review or synthesis roles.
  Suggestion: Reseat through the authoritative selection path — re-run assign_models / the static-availability application (preflight.py:1365) against the quarantine-filtered candidate set, preserving pins and explicit pools — and treat _escalate_dev_model as an unrelated capability-escalation helper.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 adds the reroute pass *before* each dispatch, but nothing intercepts the refusal *after* it. A first live refusal on DEV iteration 1 returns a non-transient startup_failure result — _is_transient_dev_failure (dev_phase.py:329) deliberately returns False for startup_failure — so dev_phase's generic failure path ends the story before any later iteration's pass can reseat, and plan_flow terminates on an unsuccessful plan result the same way. - [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 still builds the all-quarantined refusal 'via the existing _capability_refusal_result/_stamp_configured_identity pattern'. - [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1's parity test still covers only 'a profile with a transport fallback already applied'. profile_dispatch_key applies _apply_transport_fallback(profile, config.transport_fallbacks) itself (model_availability.py:272), so a run_agent caller passing a pre-fallback profile would record under a key the Step 4 overlay and catalog answers never use — the seam guard would still hold (guard and record share the key) while routing exclusion and the phase-empty stop silently miss that identity.

- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Plan risk 5 is carried by design: only runner_codex classifies MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE, so an equivalent entitlement refusal through Claude, Gemini, ghaw or the API transport keeps its existing failure code and quarantines nothing.
  Suggestion: Keep the stated scope; Step 2's docstring, the observer already being wired on all five transports, and Step 7's runbook note make it a known limit needing no seam work later.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Carried residual of plan risk 3: when a dev refusal occurs with no configured fallback (the walk exhausts), the result reaches dev_phase.py as an unsuccessful non-transient failure and the story ends through the generic failure path — dev iterations are review-triggered, so there is no 'next iteration' for Step 4's pre-dispatch pass to reseat at, and Step 6's in-story reseat test as described has no implementation path to satisfy it. Same shape in plan_flow for a refused planner. Cross-story and run-level continuation still hold via the seam and overlay, which is why this is implementation-level rather than architectural.
  Suggestion: In each phase owner, intercept MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE on the result before generic failure handling: record no model judgment, reroute via the Step 4 pass, and redispatch without consuming an ordinary retry; return the routing-stop outcome only when the pass proves the phase empty.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 4's reseat-through-_escalate_dev_model is the wrong selector for the story's own example: that helper (preflight.py:907) escalates dev to a strictly more capable model and has no planner/reviewer equivalent, so it cannot pick gpt-5.4-mini after gpt-5.4 is quarantined (a downward move) nor reseat non-dev roles.
  Suggestion: Re-run the authoritative assignment/selection machinery against the quarantine-filtered availability (the same path assign_models already takes with StoryAvailability) rather than the escalation helper, preserving pins and explicit pools; use _escalate_dev_model only where escalation is actually the policy.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 4 asserts a NoAvailableModelError from a phase-owner call becomes the SKIPPED routing stop, and engine.py does have four existing handlers (1473, 1604, 1944, 2044), but the plan does not verify the new raise sites — before a mid-story dev redispatch, a review-pool member retry, or an ancillary flow — fall inside one of them; a raise escaping to sprint/runner.py's worker-exception handling records FAILED, contradicting the stated outcome.
  Suggestion: Trace which coordinator regions the four handlers cover and wrap any uncovered new call site with the same conversion to ROUTING_STOPPED_ERROR_TYPE; make Step 6's nothing-left test raise from a later-phase pass, not initial routing.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 3 still builds the all-quarantined refusal 'via the existing _capability_refusal_result/_stamp_configured_identity pattern' without saying the SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED marker text (cli.py:224) is replaced — that marker is what agent_failure/sprint.rca classify as a capability gap, so reusing it verbatim attributes an account-entitlement refusal to the capability record, the misattribution the runbook's availability-gate section explicitly forbids.
  Suggestion: Add a sibling constructor keeping the shape (startup_failure=True, cost_usd=None, exit_code=-1, stamped identity) but carrying MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE and its own marker text; assert in tests that the story records SKIPPED/routing with no capability or assignment history written.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 1's drift test still only covers 'a profile with a transport fallback already applied' — profile_dispatch_key applies _apply_transport_fallback(profile, config.transport_fallbacks) (model_availability.py:272) before keying, so a run_agent caller passing a pre-fallback profile would record under a key the Step 4 overlay and catalog answers never use: the seam guard holds (guard and record share the key) but routing exclusion and the phase-empty stop silently miss that identity.
  Suggestion: Add the pre-fallback parity case to the Step 1 test so a mismatch fails loudly, and either normalize inside runtime_dispatch_key or verify each run_agent caller passes a post-fallback profile (routed profiles do via assignment.py/_agent_to_profile and preflight.py:996).
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Carried plan risk 5 by design: only runner_codex classifies MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE, so an equivalent entitlement refusal through the Claude, Gemini, ghaw or API transports keeps its existing failure code and quarantines nothing; the remainder-of-run criterion holds fully only on the Codex path. The plan makes this a stated scope with the observer pre-wired on all five transports so a future classifier needs no seam work, which is reasonable given the incident shape is Codex ChatGPT-account specific.
  Suggestion: Keep the agent_types.py docstring and Step 7 runbook scope statements as planned; no further plan change needed for this story.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

claims.claim: When phase names are validated from a hand-maintained list instead of deriving from actual dispatch sites, the newest dispatched phase becomes unnameable in routing.phase_eligibility until a separate source edit adds it.

Fixing phase-vocabulary drift exposed a second coupling in knowledge-summary selection: preserving the plan-derived profile matters because fallback transport, budget, timeout, and role identity can be lost if agent-pool selection overrides it.
Guard tests against future phase drift are themselves prone to drift when they enumerate a fixed set of source files or apply incomplete literal-detection rules.
Validation messaging for operator-named phases must distinguish unrecognized phases from deliberately closed ones, or the loader can suggest a remediation it will not actually accept.
Helper APIs added during a registry refactor can remain disconnected unless call sites or tests are updated to exercise them directly.

(1) A quarantine-aware *rerouting pass* runs immediately before every phase/role dispatch: it re-resolves availability with the quarantine merged, re-filters the runtime pools and phase profiles through the existing `_apply_static_availability`/`_escalate_dev_model` machinery, and raises the existing `NoAvailableModelError` when a phase has nothing left — so a refusal reseats onto a remaining model inside the same story and an emptied phase produces the #2950 `✗ ROUTING` stop, not a generic agent failure. (2) The seam in `runners/cli.py` stays as the backstop that makes 'no later story, phase or role routes to it' mechanical rather than owed to complete instrumentation. That seam is now **per raw transport call**, not at the single identity-stamping convergence: each of the five raw dispatches is observed the instant it returns and before any fallback can replace its result, and `_maybe_run_api_fallback` guards and observes each fallback candidate under that candidate's own key. Layer 1 keeps the run going; layer 2 guarantees nothing is ever paid for twice, even on a path layer 1 missed.

steps.description: Run-scoped quarantine registry with a re-entrant run scope, and a config-free dispatch key.
steps.details:
Add `runtime_dispatch_key(profile: ModelProfile) -> str | None` that builds the same string `dispatch_key` builds, from the profile alone: `canonical_model_id( provider_family, model, transport.kind)` plus transport.kind, transport.runner, provider_family, base_url. No config, no registry lookup (identity is not part of the key). Returns None on any unreadable field, never raises. Test asserts it is byte-identical to `profile_dispatch_key(profile, config)` for a profile with a transport fallback already applied, so the two surfaces cannot drift. A second test asserts a profile built by `_build_api_fallback_profile`/`_build_fallback_profile` (cli.py:281, cli.py:~330) yields a key *distinct* from its CLI parent's — the fallback dispatches a different identity and must quarantine separately.
Add `ModelQuarantine`, modelled on `AvailabilityWarnings` (same file, lines 663-754): `threading.Lock`, API `record(key, *, model, reason, auth_mode, checked_at)` storing a synthetic `ModelAvailability` with state=unavailable and freshness=current; `answer(key)`; `answers()`; `revision()`, a monotonic counter bumped on each newly added key. `record` returns True only the first time a key is added, so exactly one ROUTING line is logged per identity per run.
Scope is a **re-entrant context manager**, not a bare `reset`: `scope(run_key)` clears and claims the registry when no scope is active, and is a no-op that returns the same token when one already is. This is required, not stylistic: `sprint/runner.py:2150` calls `run_task` once *per story*, so a per-`run_task` reset would wipe the quarantine between stories and reintroduce exactly the repetition the criterion forbids. Re-entrancy lets the outermost owner (a sprint, or a CLI command) own the scope while inner owners still guarantee one exists. Exiting the outermost scope clears the registry. Expose singleton `MODEL_QUARANTINE`.
Tests: nested scopes clear once and survive the inner exit; two sequential outermost scopes in one process do not share state; concurrent `record` of the same key from two threads returns True exactly once.
This is runtime evidence, not configuration: nothing is written to ForgeConfig, no profile is mutated, nothing reaches `resolved_config_payload`. Provenance regression asserts the config digest is unchanged after a record.

steps.description: A runner-agnostic failure code for account/model entitlement refusals.
steps.details:
Define `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE = "model_unavailable_to_account"` in agent_types.py with a docstring stating plainly that only the Codex ChatGPT-account refusal shape is classified today, and that this is the hook point for the next runner — the acceptance criterion is runner-neutral, the available evidence is not.
In runner_codex.py the 400/invalid_request_error detection at lines 466-565 already exists and already cites the gpt-5.4 message. Keep it producing `PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE` for the general case. Add a narrower predicate that upgrades to the new code only when the message carries all three of: the selected model identifier, a not-supported/unsupported phrasing, and account/auth context ("with a ChatGPT account"). Anything short of all three stays on the existing code — a malformed request must never quarantine a model. Tests both ways: the exact incident message upgrades; a generic 400 invalid_request_error does not.
The code is set on `AgentResult.failure_code` (agent_types.py:171), which is what step 3's observer reads — it never re-parses provider text.

steps.description: Observe every raw transport return before any fallback can replace it; make the existing fallback walk quarantine-aware.
steps.details:
**The observation point is each raw transport return, not the identity-stamping convergence.** Verified in the tree: `run_agent` calls `_run_codex` at cli.py:700, hands that raw result to `_maybe_run_api_fallback` at cli.py:709, and only reaches `_fill_invocation_identity` at cli.py:720. A successful API fallback *replaces* the result, so the CLI entitlement refusal is gone by the convergence and the refused ChatGPT-auth identity would never be quarantined. The claude (666/676), gemini (725/734) and ghaw (760) branches and the api-only branch (652) have the same shape.
Add one private helper in cli.py:

  `_observe_dispatch(result: AgentResult, profile: ModelProfile) -> AgentResult`

— returns `result` unchanged (never swallows, never raises); when `result.failure_code == MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE`, derives `runtime_dispatch_key(profile)` and calls `MODEL_QUARANTINE.record(...)` with the profile's model label, the refusal reason, the auth mode in force for that profile, and the current timestamp; on first record emits the `⚠ ROUTING <label> excluded` line. Wrap the body so a bookkeeping error can never turn a real AgentResult into an exception.
Call it **immediately after each raw transport call, before anything else touches the result**: - api branch: after `runner_api.run_api_agent` (cli.py:652), before
  `_fill_invocation_identity`.
- claude: after `_run_claude` (cli.py:666), before the `_maybe_run_api_fallback`
  at 676.
- codex: after `_run_codex` (cli.py:700), before the `_maybe_run_api_fallback`
  at 709.
- gemini: after `_run_gemini` (cli.py:725), before the `_maybe_run_api_fallback`
  at 734.
- ghaw: after `_run_ghaw` (cli.py:760).
**Inside `_maybe_run_api_fallback` (cli.py:347)** — it dispatches identities `run_agent` never sees, so both the guard and the observation belong here, keyed by each candidate's own profile: - Before dispatching a candidate (the `api_fallback_profile` built at cli.py:281,
  then each resolved `profile.fallback_models` entry), compute that candidate's
  `runtime_dispatch_key` and skip it when quarantined — reusing the existing
  "candidate did not resolve" path so the walk simply moves to the next entry and,
  if none remain, `_annotate_cli_result` reports why nothing was attempted (extend
  `_fallback_unavailable_reason` to name quarantine as the cause).
- After each candidate dispatch, call `_observe_dispatch(candidate_result,
  candidate_profile)`.

**Teach the walk to fire on this code.** In `_classify_cli_fallback_decision` (cli.py:248), return a decision for `failure_code == MODEL_UNAVAILABLE_TO_ACCOUNT_CODE` with `cli_quota_error_observed=False` — this is the same shape as the existing `_CLI_MODEL_FALLBACK_PATTERNS` (model-not-found) branch: the identity cannot serve, the configured fallback can. This is what retires carried Risk 2 without writing a second fallback ordering anywhere.
**Guarding at entry** (`run_agent`, cli.py:608): derive `runtime_dispatch_key(profile)`. If it is quarantined, do not dispatch the primary transport and do not return immediately — build the synthetic refusal via the existing `_capability_refusal_result`/`_stamp_configured_identity` pattern (`startup_failure=True`, `cost_usd=None`, the new failure code) and pass it into `_maybe_run_api_fallback` exactly as a live refusal would be. The walk above then reseats onto the first non-quarantined configured fallback, or — when every configured identity for this call is quarantined — returns the annotated synthetic refusal with no transport invoked and nothing paid. For the api-only branch (cli.py:640) and ghaw (cli.py:747), which have no fallback walk, the guard returns that synthetic refusal directly.
That synthetic result is the backstop for a path step 4's pass does not cover, not the intended outcome: step 4 is what keeps the phase alive. The code on it is what lets phase owners classify it as a routing outcome rather than an agent failure (step 4), which matters because `_is_transient_dev_failure` (dev_phase.py:337) deliberately returns False for `startup_failure` and would otherwise end the story as an ordinary dev failure.
`run_agent_pool` needs no change — both its paths (cli.py:839, 872) call `run_agent`.
Tests (the first is the regression for this finding): - a fake codex transport returns the incident message **and** a configured API
  fallback succeeds: the call reports success, and the *CLI* identity is
  quarantined — asserting the record survives result replacement;
- the same case for claude and gemini, and for a raw api-branch refusal; - a second call with the same primary profile does not touch the primary transport
  and dispatches a non-quarantined `fallback_models` entry;
- a fallback candidate that is itself refused quarantines under the *fallback*
  profile's key, not the primary's;
- with primary and every fallback quarantined, the call returns the synthetic
  refusal and invokes no transport at all;
- a different identity is unaffected; a generic 400 quarantines nothing; - two threads dispatching the same refused identity record once and log once.

steps.description: A quarantine-aware rerouting pass immediately before every phase/role dispatch.
steps.details:
In `resolve_story_availability`, overlay `MODEL_QUARANTINE.answers()` onto the catalog result, one-directional: the quarantine can only move an identity to unavailable, never toward available. Hand-marked retired entries and the account catalog keep their existing precedence; no source overrides another toward available.
In preflight.py, beside `_apply_static_availability` and `_escalate_dev_model`, add `reroute_for_quarantine(config, state, phase) -> ForgeConfig`. It reads `MODEL_QUARANTINE.revision()` under the registry lock, returns `config` unchanged when it has not advanced since the value stamped on `CoordinatorState`, and otherwise re-resolves availability, re-runs the existing filter-then-refuse application for that phase, reselects the phase profile through `_escalate_dev_model`/`_find_registry_key_for_profile` when the currently selected one is quarantined, re-reads the revision after the merge (so an in-flight story cannot pin a pre-refusal snapshot), and raises the existing `NoAvailableModelError` when the phase has nothing left. Change `story_availability_for` (preflight.py:1289) to stamp and compare that revision alongside the cached `CoordinatorState.model_availability` rather than returning any stashed answer unconditionally.
This deliberately writes no new reseat logic — pool filtering, phase refusal, `✗ ROUTING no model available for phase ...` rendering and SKIPPED-not-FAILED recording are all existing #2950 behaviour reached with one more source merged in.
Call it immediately before each dispatch, which is the set of owners that hold a candidate set: - preflight_flow.py — before the primary dispatch and again before the configured
  fallback at line 644, matching the reseat it already performs on an availability
  answer (line 427).
- plan_flow.py — before the PLAN and PLAN_REVIEW dispatches. - dev_phase.py — before **each** DEV iteration's dispatch, so a reviewer-triggered
  second iteration cannot re-present a model refused on the first.
- review_pool.py — before each pool member's dispatch and before each per-reviewer
  retry, so one identity configured as both the dev profile and a pool member is
  dispatched once and reseated thereafter.
- escalation_advisor_flow.py and knowledge_summary_flow.py — same call in
  best-effort mode: a `NoAvailableModelError` here skips the ancillary dispatch
  with a logged reason instead of stopping a run whose real work is done.

A `NoAvailableModelError` raised from a phase-owner call is the routing stop the criterion asks for: the story is recorded SKIPPED/routing with the exclusions named, and nothing is written to capability history, assignment history or adaptive memory.

steps.description: Own the run scope at every public run owner, sprint and standalone alike.
steps.details:
Outermost owners enter `MODEL_QUARANTINE.scope(...)`: - sprint/runner.py:5365 — `scope(f"sprint:{_ctx.resolved.name}")` around the whole
  sprint, beside the existing `AVAILABILITY_WARNINGS.reset`, so the quarantine spans
  stories exactly as the criterion requires.
- cli/run.py — around the `run_task` / `run_from_dev` / `run_from_review` calls at
  lines 261-298, keyed on the run identifier, and extended to cover the post-run
  knowledge-summary dispatch that cli/shared.py reaches via
  `maybe_generate_run_summary` (shared.py:29) so that dispatch inherits the same
  scope rather than running outside any.
- cli/review.py:113 and cli/baseline_fix.py:137 — the two other standalone owners
  that call an engine entrypoint directly.

Inner backstop: `run_task`, `run_from_dev`, `run_from_review` and `run_review_only` in engine.py each enter the same scope keyed on their own run identifier. Because `scope` is re-entrant (step 1), this is a no-op inside a sprint or a CLI-owned run — the sprint's scope stays claimed across all its stories — and it guarantees any future or embedded caller still gets a clean, isolated scope. Also stamp the initial quarantine revision on `CoordinatorState` here so step 4's comparison has a baseline.
Tests: two sequential standalone `run_task` calls in one process do not share quarantine state; a sprint's quarantine *does* persist across its stories despite each story calling `run_task`; a post-run knowledge-summary dispatch after a refusal is excluded rather than re-refused.

steps.description: Seam and end-to-end tests.
steps.details: Two-story sprint: story one's dev dispatch is refused; story two's routing excludes that identity and selects the remaining model, and the sprint continues. Fallback-masked refusal (end-to-end form of the step-3 regression): story one's dev dispatch is refused at the CLI and *succeeds* via its configured API fallback, so the story passes — and story two still excludes the refused CLI identity, proving the record was taken before the fallback replaced the result. In-story reseat: the refused dev dispatch in story one does **not** end the story — the step-4 pass before the next iteration reselects a remaining model and the story completes; assert it is not recorded as a dev failure. Same-story dual-role: one identity configured both as the dev profile and as a review-pool member is dispatched once and reseated thereafter; a reviewer refused on iteration 1 is not re-dispatched on iteration 2. No-read concurrency: story two is already past its post-plan routing checkpoint when story one records the refusal — its next REVIEW dispatch still excludes the identity via the step-4 pass, and if that pass is stubbed out the step-3 seam still refuses it without reaching the transport, proving the backstop is independent of any read. Configured-fallback case: a quarantined primary with a callable `fallback_models` entry dispatches the fallback rather than failing (the carried Risk 2). Nothing-left case: the next dispatch stops with the `✗ ROUTING ... $0.00 spent` line naming the exclusions, records SKIPPED not FAILED, and writes no capability or assignment history. Ancillary: escalation-advisor and knowledge-summary dispatches inherit the quarantine; a routing stop there skips the dispatch without failing the run. Regression: an unverified identity stays fully eligible and routes until an explicit refusal converts it; a packaged retired entry stays non-routable regardless.

steps.description: Document the quarantine in the runbook's availability-gate section.
steps.details: Extend '### Model availability gate (issue #2950)' (runbook line 92) with a sixth property: an explicit refusal outranks any prior state, including unverified, and quarantines that dispatch identity for the remainder of the run. Say what the operator sees — the phase reseats onto a remaining model in the same story where one exists, a configured fallback is preferred before anything is called a stop, and a phase with nothing left produces the existing `✗ ROUTING` stop with SKIPPED-not- FAILED recording rather than a repeated provider 400. State explicitly that a transport fallback which *rescues* a refused CLI dispatch still quarantines the CLI identity — the run succeeds and the refused identity is still withheld from later dispatches, which is what the operator sees in the ROUTING line of a story that otherwise passed. State the run scope (a sprint shares one quarantine across its stories; each standalone run gets its own) and the Codex-only classification scope.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Three states; unavailable logged and excluded, unverified fully eligible and warned once.
criteria_mapping.note: Shipped by #2950; steps 4 and 6 preserve it under the overlay.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Availability resolved for the account and auth mode the run dispatches with, never as a fixed property of the identifier.
A phase left with nothing stops the run before any spend, naming exclusions.
Resolution needs no generative request and no operator action.
A config-property refusal quarantines for the remainder of the run; no later story, phase or role routes to it; the run continues on remaining models.
Hand-marked retired entries stay non-routable; neither source overrides toward availability.
Answers carry the time obtained; stale answers refreshed or reported.

risks.description: A refusal can be masked by a successful transport fallback, so observing only the value run_agent returns records nothing.
risks.mitigation: Retired in step 3: observation moved to each raw transport return, ahead of `_maybe_run_api_fallback`; fallback candidates are observed separately under their own dispatch keys. Two tests pin it — a CLI refusal rescued by API fallback still quarantines the CLI identity, and a refused fallback quarantines the fallback key, not the primary's.

risks.description: A generic 400 invalid_request_error means a malformed request, not an entitlement refusal.
risks.mitigation: Three-signal predicate (model id + unsupported phrasing + account context); everything else stays on the existing pre-generation refusal code, with a negative test. The cli.py observer reads `failure_code` only and never re-parses provider text.

risks.description: A refused dispatch could end a story that still has models left, because startup_failure is not transient.
risks.mitigation: Step 4's pass runs before each dispatch and reseats through the existing filter/reselect machinery; step 3 routes a quarantined primary into the existing `_maybe_run_api_fallback` walk rather than failing at entry, so a configured fallback is preferred; the residual synthetic result carries a code phase owners classify as a routing stop, and step 6 asserts the story completes rather than failing.

risks.description: Step 4 instruments six dispatch owners, and a seventh could be added later without one.
risks.mitigation: That is why the seam in step 3 exists: a missed owner can at worst fail its phase, never pay for the same refusal twice. Test 6's stubbed-pass case pins the backstop independently.

risks.description: Only Codex classifies the code today, so a Claude or API entitlement refusal will not quarantine.
risks.mitigation: Stated scope, not a gap found later: the code is runner-agnostic in agent_types.py with a docstring naming the hook point, the cli.py observer is already wired on all five transports so a future classifier needs no seam work, and step 7 records the limit in the runbook.

risks.description: A process-level singleton could leak across runs, or be cleared mid-sprint.
risks.mitigation: Re-entrant scope owned by the outermost run owner (sprint, or CLI command incl. post-run summary), with a nested no-op scope in every engine entrypoint. Tests cover both directions: two standalone runs isolated, one sprint's stories shared.

plan.approach: Keep the existing account-catalog availability gate as the source of pre-dispatch truth, and add only the missing run-scoped feedback loop: when a dispatch proves a model is unavailable to the active account, record that dispatch identity as unavailable for the rest of the sprint and merge it into later routing resolutions. Treat the live refusal as stronger than catalog answers, but leave unverified/catalog-failure behavior unchanged.

steps.description: Add a runtime availability override channel that routing can consume without changing model identity records.
steps.details: Add a default-empty, runtime-only availability override map to ForgeConfig keyed by the existing dispatch_key identity. Update resolve_story_availability to merge those overrides after resolve_model_availability returns, so a run-scoped unavailable answer overrides available/unverified catalog answers while packaged retired identities and normal catalog resolution keep their current behavior. Ensure the synthetic answer is a ModelAvailability with state=unavailable, checked_at set when the refusal was observed, freshness=current, and a reason that names the provider refusal.

steps.description: Classify account/model entitlement refusals separately from generic pre-generation 400 refusals.
steps.details: Introduce a shared failure code for model unavailable to the active account. Keep the existing provider_refused_before_generation cost behavior for all qualifying 400 invalid_request_error responses, but have runner_codex assign the new failure code only when the refusal text indicates the account/auth mode cannot call the selected model, such as the Codex ChatGPT-account unsupported-model message. Leave generic invalid request refusals on the existing failure code so malformed requests do not quarantine a model.

steps.description: Create a sprint-owned quarantine helper for refused dispatch identities.
steps.details: Add a small thread-safe helper owned by SprintExecutionState that inspects CoordinatorResult AgentResult fields already present on CoordinatorState: preflight_result, plan_results, plan_review_results, dev_results, and review_agent_results. When it sees the new account/model refusal failure code, resolve the refused result back to the actual dispatched profile using result.profile_name/model_used/transport_used and the result runtime_config, derive the existing availability_target and dispatch_key, and store the synthetic unavailable ModelAvailability. Expose methods to apply the current quarantine to a ForgeConfig via dataclasses.replace and to return log/audit-safe details for newly quarantined models.

steps.description: Wire the quarantine through sprint dispatch boundaries and outcome handling.
steps.details: Add the quarantine helper to SprintExecutionState, and apply it immediately before each existing coordinator entrypoint that can dispatch a model: run_task, run_from_dev, run_from_review, and run_review_only, including the plan-gate continuation path and batch-group member reviews. After each CoordinatorResult returns, observe it before scheduling more work, log a ROUTING warning for newly quarantined identities, mark that story as skipped/routing rather than a story failure when the only terminal cause was the account/model refusal, and do not trigger the existing sprint-wide routing_stop unless a later availability-filtered routing pass raises NoAvailableModelError because no available or unverified candidate remains.

steps.description: Add seam tests for the run-scoped feedback loop and preserve existing availability semantics.
steps.details: Cover a two-story sprint where the first story receives the account/model refusal and the second story's routing excludes that same dispatch identity and selects the remaining model. Add a no-remaining-models case that stops before the next dispatch with the existing RoutingStopped path, a plan-gate or batch-member continuation case proving quarantine is consulted at later phase boundaries, and a regression that unverified catalog answers remain eligible until an explicit live refusal converts that dispatch identity to unavailable for the rest of the run.

criteria_mapping.criterion: Every configured model resolves to exactly one of three states: available, unavailable, or unverified; unavailable is logged and excluded, unverified remains fully eligible and warns once.
Availability is resolved for the account and authentication mode the run will dispatch with, not as a fixed property of the model identifier.
A phase left with no available or unverified model stops the run before any spend, naming excluded models and reasons.
Resolution completes without dispatching a generative request and without the operator running anything.
A config-property dispatch refusal quarantines that model for the remainder of the run, including unverified models, and later stories/phases/roles continue on remaining models.
Entries already marked withdrawn by hand in the packaged catalog remain non-routable, and neither source overrides the other toward availability.
An availability answer carries the time it was obtained, and stale answers older than the identity-verification window are refreshed or reported stale rather than reused as current.

risks.description: A generic HTTP 400 invalid_request_error can mean a malformed request, not an account/model entitlement refusal.
risks.mitigation: Use the new quarantine failure code only for narrow account/model unsupported text; keep broad pre-generation refusal handling limited to cost classification.

risks.description: Parallel workers may already have dispatched the refused model before the first refusal is observed.
risks.mitigation: Define quarantine as affecting all subsequent dispatch boundaries, and apply it again at plan-gate continuations and batch member reviews so queued-but-not-yet-dispatched phases do not reuse stale config.

risks.description: Mapping a refused AgentResult back to a dispatch identity can be ambiguous when fallback transports or aliases are involved.
risks.mitigation: Prefer result.model_used and result.transport_used when present, fall back to the matched runtime profile, and derive the final key through the existing availability_target and dispatch_key helpers rather than by model string.

plan.approach: Keep the existing account-catalog availability gate as the source of pre-dispatch truth, but move the missing feedback loop to a shared run-scoped availability registry outside ForgeConfig. When any dispatch proves a model is unavailable to the active account/auth mode, the coordinator records that dispatch identity immediately, availability reads merge the registry with catalog answers, and later story/phase/role dispatches route around it. Treat live refusals as stronger than catalog answers, while leaving unverified/catalog-failure behavior unchanged.

steps.description: Add a shared run-scoped availability quarantine registry outside ForgeConfig.
steps.details: Create a small thread-safe RunModelAvailabilityQuarantine/registry in model_availability.py, following the existing run-scoped auth/cancellation state pattern rather than adding fields to ForgeConfig. Key entries by the existing dispatch_key identity derived from availability_target, store a synthetic ModelAvailability with state=unavailable, checked_at set when the refusal was observed, freshness=current, and a reason naming the provider refusal. Expose methods to record a refused identity, merge current quarantines into a StoryAvailability/availability result, return a monotonic revision for cache invalidation, and provide log/audit-safe newly-quarantined details. Do not serialize quarantine state as resolved configuration; add a provenance/digest regression proving refusal timestamps and reasons do not affect resolved_config_payload or the config digest.

steps.description: Merge quarantine at the availability-read point and invalidate cached story availability when it changes.
steps.details: Update resolve_story_availability and story_availability_for so every read combines packaged retired status, account-catalog resolution, and run-scoped quarantine entries, with quarantine only able to move a dispatch identity toward unavailable. Track the quarantine revision on cached CoordinatorState model availability; when the registry revision changes, re-merge or re-resolve instead of reusing stale state.model_availability. Preserve the existing semantics that unavailable catalog answers are logged and excluded, unverified answers remain fully eligible and warn once, stale catalog answers older than the identity-verification window are refreshed or reported stale, and packaged retired entries remain non-routable.

steps.description: Classify account/model entitlement refusals with a runner-agnostic failure code and narrow Codex matching.
steps.details: Define a runner-agnostic failure code/helper for model unavailable to the active account so other runners can adopt it later. In runner_codex, keep the existing provider_refused_before_generation cost behavior for qualifying 400 invalid_request_error responses, but assign the new failure code only when the message is anchored on stable fragments: the selected model name, a not-supported/unsupported condition, and account/auth context such as Codex with ChatGPT-account authentication. Leave unmatched or generic invalid request refusals on the existing PRE_GENERATION_REFUSAL_CODE so malformed requests do not quarantine a model. Add positive and negative classification tests showing the Codex ChatGPT-account unsupported-model refusal quarantines, while an unmatched 400 degrades to current behavior.

steps.description: Record refusals immediately at shared coordinator dispatch/result seams.
steps.details: Pass the run-scoped quarantine registry through coordinator state/context for both sprint-owned runs and standalone forge run. After every AgentResult-producing dispatch returns, including preflight, plan, plan review, dev iterations, review pool members, escalation advisor calls, and knowledge summary calls, inspect the result immediately. When it carries the account/model refusal failure code, resolve the actual dispatched profile using result.profile_name/model_used/transport_used plus runtime_config, derive availability_target and dispatch_key through existing helpers, record the synthetic unavailable answer, and emit ROUTING warning details for newly quarantined identities. Because the coordinator records the refusal before continuing, later roles inside the same run_task call and surviving plan-review quorum paths already see the quarantine.

steps.description: Wire sprint and batch-preflight boundaries to share and observe the same quarantine.
steps.details: Add the shared quarantine registry to SprintExecutionState and pass it into every coordinator entrypoint: run_task, run_from_dev, run_from_review, run_review_only, plan-gate continuations, batch-group member reviews, and the batch preflight pass. In run_batch_preflight, observe each CoordinatorResult before collapsing failed preflight state so refusals are not discarded. Keep applying the registry at sprint entrypoints for cross-story coverage, but rely on coordinator availability reads for in-flight phases. When a story hits a config-property entitlement refusal, prefer re-entering/rerouting that story under the quarantined availability state when the coordinator can safely continue; if it cannot be retried, mark it SKIPPED/routing, write nothing to capability or assignment history, and continue the sprint. Do not trigger sprint-wide routing_stop unless a later availability-filtered routing pass raises NoAvailableModelError because no available or unverified candidate remains.

steps.description: Add seam tests for same-story, cross-story, standalone, ancillary, and concurrency behavior.
steps.details: Cover a two-story sprint where the first story receives the account/model refusal and the second story's routing excludes that dispatch identity and selects the remaining model. Add an unsplit run_task case where a plan-review refusal is followed by a later role using the same identity, proving the later role routes around it before sprint/runner.py observes the full CoordinatorResult. Add standalone forge run coverage, ancillary dispatch coverage for escalation advisor or knowledge summary calls, and a batch preflight case proving a refusal observed during run_batch_preflight is retained for story workers. Add a concurrent two-story case where one story records the refusal while another is mid-story, proving the next availability read in the in-flight story consults the updated quarantine. Include no-remaining-models coverage that stops before the next dispatch with the existing RoutingStopped path, and a regression that unverified catalog answers remain eligible until an explicit live refusal converts that dispatch identity to unavailable for the rest of the run. Assert that quarantine-caused SKIPPED/routing stories write no capability/assignment history and that rerouted stories continue on remaining models when safe.

steps.description: Record at the shared dispatch seam; guard without stranding configured fallbacks.
steps.details:
Recording (the part that must never be missed): after each transport returns — the claude, codex, gemini, ghaw and api branches all converge on `_fill_invocation_identity`/`_stamp_configured_identity` — classify the result; on the new failure code call `MODEL_QUARANTINE.record(...)` keyed by the profile that actually produced it, and on first record emit the `⚠ ROUTING <label> excluded` line. steps.description: A quarantine-aware rerouting pass immediately before every phase/role dispatch.
steps.details:
In `resolve_story_availability`, overlay `MODEL_QUARANTINE.answers()` onto the catalog result, one-directional: the quarantine can only move an identity to unavailable, never toward available. Hand-marked retired entries and the account catalog keep their existing precedence; no source overrides another toward available.
In preflight.py, beside `_apply_static_availability` and `_escalate_dev_model`, add `reroute_for_quarantine(config, state, phase) -> ForgeConfig`. It reads `MODEL_QUARANTINE.revision()` under the registry lock, returns `config` unchanged when it has not advanced since the value stamped on `CoordinatorState`, and otherwise re-resolves availability, re-runs the existing filter-then-refuse application for that phase, reselects the phase profile through `_escalate_dev_model`/`_find_registry_key_for_profile` when the currently selected one is quarantined, re-reads the revision after the merge (so an in-flight story cannot pin a pre-refusal snapshot), and raises the existing `NoAvailableModelError` when the phase has nothing left. Change `story_availability_for` (preflight.py:1289) to stamp and compare that revision alongside the cached `CoordinatorState.model_availability` rather than returning any stashed answer unconditionally.
This deliberately writes no new reseat logic — pool filtering, phase refusal, `✗ ROUTING no model available for phase ...` rendering and SKIPPED-not-FAILED recording are all existing #2950 behaviour reached with one more source merged in.
Call it immediately before each dispatch, which is the set of owners that hold a candidate set: - preflight_flow.py — before the primary dispatch and again before the configured
  fallback at line 644, matching the reseat it already performs on an availability
  answer (line 427).
- plan_flow.py — before the PLAN and PLAN_REVIEW dispatches. - dev_phase.py — before **each** DEV iteration's dispatch, so a reviewer-triggered
  second iteration cannot re-present a model refused on the first.
- review_pool.py — before each pool member's dispatch and before each per-reviewer
  retry, so one identity configured as both the dev profile and a pool member is
  dispatched once and reseated thereafter.
- escalation_advisor_flow.py and knowledge_summary_flow.py — same call in
  best-effort mode: a `NoAvailableModelError` here skips the ancillary dispatch
  with a logged reason instead of stopping a run whose real work is done.

A `NoAvailableModelError` raised from a phase-owner call is the routing stop the criterion asks for: the story is recorded SKIPPED/routing with the exclusions named, and nothing is written to capability history, assignment history or adaptive memory.

  that call an engine entrypoint directly.
